newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency rejects Canadian power marketing bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency rejects Canadian power marketing bid.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) this week turned down an application by Powerex, the marketing arm of Canadian state utility B.C. Hydro, for status as a power marketer in the U.S.
"This simply means to us business as usual," a spokeswoman for Powerex in Vancouver said Thursday.
The trading firm plans to continue selling power at the U.S. Canada border, where title is then transferred to U.S. buyers who arrange their own transmission, Sheena Macdonald said.
With status as a power marketer in the U.S., Powerex would have been able to sell electricity directly to U.S. buyers and to buy and sell power within U.S.
But FERC turned the application down based on concerns about open transmission access into Canada for U.S. power suppliers, Macdonald said.
"We are assessing what our options will be," she added.
